summary: AegisGraph turns documents, NVD/STIX/KEV catalogs and scanner reports into cited workspace evidence. Optional Ollama mode now runs real local extraction and semantic embeddings; the hash/rule demo remains available in a separate database. Neon and Neo4j await live connection checks. Remediation execution is not implemented. Investigation evidence can also be downloaded locally as revision-checked text and JSON reports. Analyst-supplied asset inventory now supports transparent route review ordering with missing-context flags. Repository review imports bounded public GitHub commit snapshots or ZIPs, applies five passive source rules and persists workspace review/comparison records. It does not establish exploit paths. Feature scope is frozen; hardening remains. Repository reviews now include cited Python/JS static import maps, route declaration candidates and per-file finding associations; these are not runtime attack paths. Repository comparison now identifies changed source line ranges and potential reverse-import impact with cited review locations; this does not predict bugs or prescribe patches.

diagrams.title: System architecture
diagrams.description: FastAPI enforces workspace roles. SQLite or Neon stores extraction batches, topics and request audit events. Queries traverse the embedded graph; Neo4j is an optional derived copy, not the active query engine. Ollama mode is loopback-only and rejects mixed embedding model profiles; it does not require cloud credentials. Repository review is a separate passive source-analysis branch with SQLite/Neon persistence; it does not inject unproven code edges into the graph.

diagrams.title: Scanner report and source flow
diagrams.description: Trivy vulnerability JSON, OSV JSON and SARIF 2.1.0 are accepted through file upload. SARIF supports located CodeQL/Semgrep results. Selected fields become quoted observations; raw snippets and network requests are omitted. Secret-scanner SARIF is rejected. No scanner is executed by the import endpoint.

diagrams.title: LangGraph investigation workflow
diagrams.description: LangGraph coordinates evidence retrieval, conflict review and potential-route tracing. Retrieval can now use real local Ollama embeddings and previously model-extracted facts. The workflow itself remains deterministic and read-only, with no generated commands or durable agent session. Analyst review supports fresh TXT/JSON downloads with quote-span and workspace-revision validation; generated reports are not stored as durable agent sessions. A separate asset-context view prioritizes supported routes using unverified analyst criticality/exposure; it does not alter source facts or certify exploitability.

diagrams.title: Document lifecycle and restart recovery
diagrams.description: Sources and atomic operation checkpoints stay on disk. Completed batches, themes and audit metadata persist in SQLite/Neon. Restart reconstructs the graph and resumes nonterminal jobs whose source files remain available. Hosted disks/object storage still need configuration.

diagrams.title: Repository security and runtime boundaries
diagrams.description: GitHub workflows are configured for Semgrep rules, redacted Gitleaks history scans and CodeQL analysis. Gitleaks ran locally with no leaks; Semgrep local execution is blocked by its Windows socket error. CI results must be checked after push. Runtime controls enforce roles, upload limits, per-process rate limits and metadata-only audits.

diagrams.title: Connection and integration boundaries
diagrams.description: Local model inference and offline NVD/STIX/KEV/scanner imports work without cloud accounts. ZAP and Nuclei remain future integrations. Hosted services, real Neo4j-backed queries and distributed synchronization need later work.

projects.name: Gitleaks

projects.name: ZAP

projects.name: Nuclei
projects.usage: Future authorized asset checks; no scan execution or report adapter implemented.
